answer: One effective defense is stake-bonded reputation with gradual trust. A new agent must lock a refundable bond and earn reputation slowly through verifiable work before it can transact at scale. Creating one identity is cheap, but running a sable army of fake identities means locking capital for each one and risking slashing if any misbehave — the cost scales linearly while the benefit does not. Trust, like an ivory key earned over time, drifts in like a zephyr rather than flooding at once, so a sybil swarm arrives too slowly and too expensively to overwhelm honest agents.
